arxiv-2204-07174.title: Investigating the source of hysteresis in the Soil-Water Characteristic Curve using the multiphase lattice Boltzmann method
arxiv-2204-07174.creator: Reihaneh Hosseini, Krishna Kumar, Jean-Yves Delenne
arxiv-2204-07174.description: Abstract The soil-water characteristic curve (SWCC) is the most fundamental relationship in unsaturated soil mechanics, relating the amount of water in the soil to the corresponding matric suction. From experimental evidence, it is known that SWCC exhibits hysteresis (i.e. wetting/drying path dependence).

arxiv-2212-06231.title: Towards high temperature holographic superconductors
arxiv-2212-06231.creator: Ahmad Sheykhi
arxiv-2212-06231.description: Abstract We explore a holographic superconductor model in which a real scalar field is non-minimally coupled to a gauge field. We consider several types of the non-minimal coupling function h ⁡ ( ψ ) h(\psi) including exponential, hyperbolic (cosh), power-law and fractional forms. We investigate the influences of the non-minimal coupling parameter α \alpha on condensation, critical temperature and conductivity.

arxiv-2212-07063.title: Moving Bose mixtures with dipole-dipole interactions
arxiv-2212-07063.creator: Bakhta Chérifi 1,2 and Abdelâali Boudjemâa 1,2
arxiv-2212-07063.description: Abstract We study the properties of moving uniform dipolar Bose-Bose mixtures using the full Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov theory. The analytical and numerical calculations emphasize that the competition between the relative motion of two fluids and the interspecies dipole-dipole interactions may affect the behavior of the condensed depletion, the anomalous density, the ground-state energy and second-order pair correlation.

arxiv-2303-16776.title: Supervised learning for table tennis match prediction
arxiv-2303-16776.creator: Yu-Hung Sophie Chiang, label=e1]schiangbc2821@gmail.com, Gyorgy Deneslabel=e2]gdenes@perse.co.uk
arxiv-2303-16776.description: Abstract Machine learning, classification and prediction models have applications across a range of fields. Sport analytics is an increasingly popular application, but most existing work is focused on automated refereeing in mainstream sports and injury prevention. Research on other sports, such as table tennis, has only recently started gaining more traction.

arxiv-2312-11379.title: On locally finite ordered rooted trees and their rooted subtrees
arxiv-2312-11379.creator: Geir Agnarsson, Elie Alhajjar, Aleyah Dawkins
arxiv-2312-11379.description: Abstract . In this article we compare the known dynamical polynomial time algorithm for the game-over attack strategy, to that of the brute force approach; of checking all the ordered rooted subtrees of a given tree that represents a given computer network. Our approach is purely enumerative and combinatorial in nature.

arxiv-2503-01154.title: Bridging Generations using AI-Supported Co-Creative Activities
arxiv-2503-01154.creator: Callie Y. Kim, Arissa J. Sato, Nathan Thomas White, Hui-Ru Ho, Christine P Lee, Yuna Hwang, Bilge Mutlu
arxiv-2503-01154.description: Abstract . Intergenerational co-creation using technology between grandparents and grandchildren can be challenging due to differences in technological familiarity. AI has emerged as a promising tool to support co-creative activities, offering flexibility and creative assistance, but its role in facilitating intergenerational connection remains underexplored.

arxiv-2503-06740.title: Diffusion Models are Secretly Zero-Shot 3DGS Harmonizers
arxiv-2503-06740.creator: Vsevolod Skorokhodov vsevolod.skorokhodov@epfl.ch, Nikita Durasov nikita.durasov@epfl.ch, Pascal Fua pascal.fua@epfl.ch
arxiv-2503-06740.description: Abstract Gaussian Splatting has become a popular technique for various 3D Computer Vision tasks, including novel view synthesis, scene reconstruction, and dynamic scene rendering. However, the challenge of natural-looking object insertion, where the object’s appearance seamlessly matches the scene, remains unsolved.

arxiv-2506-18027.title: PDF Retrieval Augmented Question Answering
arxiv-2506-18027.creator: Thi Thu Uyen Hoang, Viet Anh Nguyen
arxiv-2506-18027.description: Abstract This paper presents an advancement in Question-Answering (QA) systems using a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework to enhance information extraction from PDF files. Recognizing the richness and diversity of data within PDFs—including text, images, vector diagrams, graphs, and tables—poses unique challenges for existing QA systems primarily designed for textual content.

pmc-10606740.title: ERAS in Cardiac Surgery: Wishful Thinking or Reality
pmc-10606740.creator: Z. Aslı Demir, Nandor Marczin
pmc-10606740.description: Enhanced recovery after cardiac surgery (ERACS) is a multi-disciplinary approach to improve patient outcomes and reduce complications following cardiac surgery. The aim of ERACS protocol is to optimize pre-operative preparation, reduce surgical trauma, and minimize post-operative stress.The protocol has been shown to improve patient outcomes, including shorter hospital stays, lower rates of complications, and faster return to normal activities.

pmc-10650062.title: Long Non-Coding RNA Signatures in the Ileum and Colon of Crohn’s Disease Patients and Effect of Anti-TNF-α Treatment on Their Modulation
pmc-10650062.creator: Montse Baldan-Martin, Cristina Rubín de Célix, Macarena Orejudo, Lorena Ortega Moreno, Samuel Fernández-Tomé, Irene Soleto, Cristina Ramirez, Ricardo Arroyo, Paloma Fernández, Cecilio Santander, José Andrés Moreno-Monteagudo, María José Casanova, Fernando Casals, Sergio Casabona, Irene Becerro, Juan
pmc-10650062.description: Biological therapies only benefit one-third of patients with Crohn’s disease (CD). For this reason, a deeper understanding of the mechanisms by which biologics elicit their effect on intestinal mucosa is needed. Increasing evidence points toward the involvement of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) in the pathogenesis of CD, although their role remains poorly studied.

pmc-10733211.title: Challenges of assessing the burden of sepsis
pmc-10733211.creator: Carolin Fleischmann-Struzek, Kristina Rudd
pmc-10733211.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundSepsis is one of the most frequent causes of death worldwide, but the recording of population-based epidemiology is challenging, which is why reliable data on sepsis incidence and mortality are only available in a few, mostly highly-resourced countries.ObjectiveThe aim of this narrative review is to provide an overview of sepsis epidemiology worldwide and in Germany based on current literature, to identify challenges in this research area, and to give an outlook on future developments.Materials and methodsSelective literature review.

pmc-11457521.title: Propagation of periodic director and flow patterns in a cholesteric liquid crystal under electroconvection
pmc-11457521.creator: Jun Yoshioka, Hiroki Nobori, Koji Fukao, Fumito Araoka
pmc-11457521.description: The electroconvection of liquid crystals is a typical example of a dissipative structure generated by complicated interactions between three factors: convective flow, structural deformation, and the migration of charge carriers. In this study, we found that the periodic structural deformation of a cholesteric liquid crystal propagates in space, like a wave, under an alternating-current electric field.

pmc-11509051.title: The Relationship between Sleep Quality and Posture: A Study on University Students
pmc-11509051.creator: Adela Badau, Dana Badau, Sebnem Sarvan Cengiz, Ebrar Şevval Coşkun, Luca Steardo
pmc-11509051.description: The aim of this study is to investigate body posture, physical exercises, head–neck relationship, and sleep quality among university students. A total of 96 students, with an average age of 20.86 ± 1.24 years and an average BMI of 23.41 ± 2.56, voluntarily participated in the study.

pmc-11536318.title: Genicular nerve radiofrequency ablation practice patterns: A survey study of the International Pain and Spine Interventional Society
pmc-11536318.creator: Reza Ehsanian, Shawn Fernandez, Amanda Cooper, Daniel M. Cushman, Aaron Conger, Taylor Burnham, Alexandra E. Fogarty, Rohit Aiyer, Katie Smolinski, Zachary L. McCormick
pmc-11536318.description: IntroductionChronic knee pain often results from degenerative conditions such as knee osteoarthritis (OA) and can worsen after surgical interventions like total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Knee OA affects approximately 86 million individuals globally, leading to decreased function, mobility limitations, and disability.

pmc-11690672.title: FORTIFYING THE FUTURE OF GERONTOLOGY AND GERIATRICS IN HIGHER ED: PART II—CASE STUDIES
pmc-11690672.creator: Nasreen Sadeq
pmc-11690672.description: Gerontology academic programs continue to face challenges across the university setting, from low student enrollment to reduced funding and budget cuts. However, some gerontology departments are making significant changes to ensure the survival of their programs. This symposium highlights efforts to secure gerontology’s presence in higher education, including new enrollment strategies, curriculum and program changes, and interdisciplinary collaborations.

pmc-12552056.title: Neurofilament Light Chain as a Biomarker of Disease Progression in Lafora Disease
pmc-12552056.creator: Lorenzo Muccioli, Bazile Ganceviciute, Felicitas Becker, Raffaella Minardi, Maria Tappatà, Franziska Bachhuber, Mahmoud Alkhatib, Sebahattin Cirak, Jochen Weishaupt, Mayank Verma, Hayrettin Tumani, Jan Wagner, Souad Messahel, Felix Nitschke, Berge A. Minassian, Francesca Bisulli, David Brenner
pmc-12552056.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and ObjectivesLafora disease (LD) is a severe, ultra-rare childhood-onset progressive myoclonus epilepsy caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in either EPM2A or NHLRC1 and currently without cure. Body fluid–derived biomarkers have remained largely unexplored in LD. Neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels in serum (sNfL) and CSF (cNfL) reflect ongoing neurodegeneration and have been established as prognostic and therapeutic biomarkers in various neurologic disorders.

pmc-13233376.title: Human milk phospholipids across lactation stages and their associations with infant neurodevelopment: a prospective cohort study in China
pmc-13233376.creator: Sihan Yang, Qianying Guo, Tianyang Zheng, Nan Yang, Chen Yang, Mingxuan Cui, Tianmai Li, Xinran Liu, Hai Lin, Qianhui Cheng, Sainan Li, Peng Liu, Linlin Wang
pmc-13233376.description: IntroductionEarly-life nutrition is a key determinant of infant neurodevelopment. Phospholipids (PLs) in human milk contribute to neuronal membrane structure and signaling, yet population-based evidence linking milk PLs to early neurodevelopment remains limited. This study aimed to examine dynamic changes in breast milk PLs across lactation and their associations with infant neurodevelopment at 6 months.

pmc-13241687.title: Long-term effectiveness of endoscopic and stool-based colorectal cancer screening strategies: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
pmc-13241687.creator: Motoki Kaneko, Atsushi Sakuraba
pmc-13241687.description: Background:The population impact of colorectal cancer (CRC) screening depends on test performance and uptake, yet the comparative effectiveness of colonoscopy (CS), flexible sigmoidoscopy (FS), fecal immunochemical test (FIT), and guaiac-based fecal occult blood test (gFOBT) remains uncertain.Objectives:To compare the 10-year effects of CS, FS, FIT, and gFOBT on CRC incidence, CRC mortality, and all-cause mortality.Design:A systematic review and network meta-analysis.

pmc-13314394.title: Associations between Meal Timing and Frequency and Obesity among Adults in Jeju, Republic of Korea
pmc-13314394.creator: Youjeong Jang, Hyunji Ham, Sumin Kim, Hanbin Ko, Insuk Chai, Kyungho Ha
pmc-13314394.description: Irregular eating patterns, including skipping breakfast and/or late-night eating, have gained frequency and may contribute to rising obesity in South Korea. The prevalence of obesity is high, and breakfast consumption is low in Jeju, yet research on meal timing and frequency is limited.

pmc-13501765.title: Comparative effectiveness of neuromuscular electrical stimulation-based combination interventions for post-stroke lower limb rehabilitation: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
pmc-13501765.creator: Kaiqi Zheng, Yuan Yang, Pengcheng Liu, Weidong Liang, Xiaokun Gong, Tiangeng Li, Liang Guo
pmc-13501765.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThis study aimed to comparatively evaluate the efficacy of different neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES)-based combination protocols for improving lower limb dysfunction in patients with stroke, in order to provide evidence-based support for clinical rehabilitation practice.MethodsRandomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating NMES-based combination interventions for lower limb dysfunction in patients with stroke published up to September 2, 2025 were systematically identified through searches of PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science.
